_doc: Fixer registry (#137, campaign epic #136). One entry == one gate-scoped
appearance; multi-stage conversations are separate entries whose
name           display name shown in the bar
base           base id placement; matches bare id or id_<suffix>
offer          offer line ('' / absent = pure dialogue)
accept_actions [..] run on ACCEPT: plot verbs or campaign tokens
done_actions   [..] run when a pure-dialogue conversation ends

fixers.name: Ernesto Sandoval
dialogue: Welcome to New Detroit. You look like a man who's hungry for work. Sandoval. Ernesto Sandoval.
A simple delivery of iron, strictly legit - forty units to the Liverpool refinery in Newcastle. Just a short jump. No contraband, no hassles.
Fifteen thousand credits on your return. I don't have it on me... but I'll show you something better. Here - hold this as collateral until I pay.
Don't ask me what it is. Just keep it safe, and keep it quiet. Bring it back with you and there's another five thousand in it for you.
fixers.offer: Haul 40 units of iron to Liverpool (Newcastle system), then return here for 15,000 credits - plus 5,000 for returning his collateral. Deal?

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: Looking for Sandoval? Don't bother. He's dead. Word is it wasn't an accident.
Name's Tayla. Sandoval owed people, and now those people are curious about that trinket he handed you as collateral.
Keep it. He's in no position to redeem it, and his fifteen grand died with him. It's yours now, like it or not.
I'll tell you this much for free: Sandoval didn't buy that thing. He got it by killing the man who owned it. Death follows it, $CS. Feel lucky?
I know more. I'll trade it out a piece at a time, and you'll earn every piece. Come see me when you're ready to work.

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: Ready to work? Good. First job's a milk run: thirty units of plastics. Completely legal, nothing to hide.
Officially you're running it to Newcastle. Actually you'll divert to Oakham - a hidden pirate base out in Pentonville. The paperwork is for anyone watching.
Oakham sits in an asteroid field, so mind your speed on approach. And relax - while you fly for me, Pentonville's pirates keep their guns to themselves.
Ten thousand on delivery. Leave the ship docked and meet me in the Oakham bar - we'll talk more there.
fixers.offer: Haul 30 units of plastics to Oakham (Pentonville system) for 10,000 credits on landing. Deal?

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: Now the real work. Brilliance - yes, THAT Brilliance - to Hector, the mining base in Troy.
The militia have Troy crawling with Talons, and they scan everything that moves. Do not stop. Do not fight. Burn past them.
Fifteen thousand on delivery at Hector. Then get yourself back here in one piece.
fixers.offer: Smuggle 15 units of Brilliance to Hector (Troy system) for 15,000 credits, then return to Oakham. In?

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: You made it past the militia with the goods AND your hull. I'm almost impressed.
Catch your breath. The next run makes Troy look like a pleasure cruise.

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: Bigger load this time: Brilliance to New Constantinople itself. Twenty-five units.
Before you ask - I bribed the Confed patrols on the route. You won't have any trouble. Trust me.
Twenty thousand on delivery. Then come straight back.
fixers.offer: Smuggle 25 units of Brilliance to New Constantinople for 20,000 credits, then return to Oakham. Deal?

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: Bribed patrols, you say? Stilettos and Broadswords at every jump point, you say? Huh. Must have been a clerical error.
Stop scowling. To make it up to you, my people just installed something in your ship: a smuggler's compartment. Twenty units, invisible to any scanner ever built.
Contraband only - the baffles foul anything legitimate. One more run and we're square.

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: Last run: twenty units of Brilliance to New Constantinople. Fits that new compartment of yours exactly. Poetic, no?
One thing. William Riordian - used to fly these runs before you showed up. He's been drinking and talking, mostly about you.
Ten thousand, and after this I'll tell you everything I know about your trinket. Watch yourself out there.
fixers.offer: One final run: 20 units of Brilliance to New Constantinople for 10,000 credits. Finish the job?

fixers.name: Tayla
dialogue: Riordian, hm? He always was a jealous idiot. You did fine.
Here's the rest of what I owe you. Before Sandoval, it belonged to a spice merchant named Deiter - who had it from his own father. Every owner I can name died holding it.
That's where my thread runs out. I've sent the holo on to someone who can actually read it: Roman Lynch, on New Constantinople. A thug, but an expert on exotic and valuable things.
He's expecting you in the bar there. That squares us. It's been profitable, pilot. Try not to die.

fixers.name: Roman Lynch
dialogue: You don't wanna talk to me, 'cause I don't wanna talk to you. Mr. Lynch, sittin' over there - HE'S the one you wanna talk to. So state your bidness or take a hike, buddy.
Enough, Miggs. Ah, Captain - I've been expecting you. I am Roman Lynch. You may speak freely around my assistant; he is exceedingly loyal.
Your artifact interests me. There's a hologram in it, did you know? My people will study it while you make yourself useful.
A certain Captain Seelig is loitering at Nav 3 in Pentonville - his ship is the Hooded Hawk. Deliver a message: tell him how profoundly disappointed I am in him. Verbatim, please.
Ten thousand when you get back. A simple courier run - what could go wrong?
fixers.offer: Deliver Lynch's message to Seelig at Pentonville Nav 3, then return to New Constantinople for 10,000 credits. Accept?

fixers.name: Roman Lynch
dialogue: Seelig took it badly? Shocking. Some men simply cannot accept a severance package.
Your ten thousand, as agreed. The hologram is... resisting analysis. My people need more time - and I have more work.

fixers.name: Roman Lynch
dialogue: The artifact investigation has hit... complications. People keep dying around it. Fascinating, really.
Meanwhile: twenty units of weaponry to Siva, the agricultural base in Rikel. Fifteen thousand on delivery.
One wrinkle. Salman Kroiz runs guns on that route and considers it his. He flies a Demon. So do his friends.
fixers.offer: Run 20 units of weaponry to Siva (Rikel system) for 15,000 credits, past Kroiz's gang. Accept?

fixers.name: Roman Lynch
dialogue: Your trinket is confirmed alien. Not Kilrathi - OLD. That knowledge cost me three good analysts.
Before we discuss it further: my cousin Regis has been subpoenaed in a murder trial. It would be best for everyone if he simply... disappeared.
He favors the Romulus mining base in Castor. Get him out of New Constantinople and take him there. Thirty thousand on landing. Do avoid the Stilettos - they are faster than you.
fixers.offer: Smuggle Lynch's cousin Regis to Romulus (Castor system) for 30,000 credits on landing. Take him aboard?

fixers.name: Roman Lynch
dialogue: One last job. A Mr. Smythe on Liverpool claims he found something about your artifact in the Oxford library archives.
Pick him up, bring him here. Thirty thousand for a taxi run. You may notice Miggs is elsewhere tonight - errands of his own.
Go on then. Liverpool. Newcastle system. Mr. Smythe is waiting.
fixers.offer: Fly to Liverpool (Newcastle system) and collect Mr. Smythe for 30,000 credits. Accept?

fixers.name: Masterson
dialogue: Ah. The pilot with the artifact and the trail of dead mobsters. Masterson, university administration. And no - the library is CLOSED to you.
However. Access can be purchased - not with money, but with service. Consider it an endowment to the university, paid in four installments. Complete them and I unlock the archive myself.
First installment: Hunter Toth is inbound in a Drayman at the Saxtogue jump point. He wrote unkind truths about the Retros, and Retros hold grudges.
Meet him there and see him to the planet. He must be ON THE GROUND before you land - I will not pay for a corpse with an honor guard.
fixers.offer: Escort Toth's Drayman from the Saxtogue Jump to Oxford for 10,000 credits. He lands first. Accept?

fixers.name: Masterson
dialogue: Favor two. Data pirates are draining our mainframe from a ship parked somewhere in-system: the Black Rhombus. A converted Galaxy, bristling with turrets.
Patrol the jump points until you find it, and make it stop existing. The escorts are optional; the Rhombus is not.
Ten thousand on your return. Do check your ammunition first.
fixers.offer: Hunt down and destroy the Black Rhombus somewhere at Oxford's jump points, then return. 10,000 credits. Accept?

fixers.name: Masterson
dialogue: Favor three. My book shipment arrives on the Drayman Vulcan's Forge at the Saxtogue jump point. A rival collector hired bounty hunters to divert it.
Here is the wrinkle: the hunters were paid to remove the ESCORT. That would be you. The Demons will ignore the freighter entirely.
Same terms: the Forge lands first, then you. Ten thousand.
fixers.offer: Escort Vulcan's Forge from the Saxtogue Jump to Oxford - the Demons will hunt YOU. 10,000 credits. Accept?

fixers.name: Masterson
dialogue: Last favor. One more Drayman, inbound at the XXN-1927 jump point, carrying... let us say 'pirate bait'. They know what is in the hold and they want it badly.
I will be honest with you, pilot: this freighter is a rust bucket. Her plating would embarrass a shuttle. Keep the Talons OFF her.
She lands first. Then you. Then the library opens. Ten thousand, and my genuine respect.
fixers.offer: Escort the final Drayman from the XXN-1927 Jump to Oxford - she is fragile and the pirates want her badly. 10,000 credits. Accept?

fixers.name: Oxford Library
dialogue: The archive terminal accepts Masterson's authorization. You place the artifact in the scanner cradle.
MATCH FOUND. Classification: STELTEK. A precursor civilization - starfaring while humanity was learning fire. No verified contact in recorded history.
The artifact is a power relay of unknown function. Energy signature: dormant, but not dead. Cross-reference: recent anomalous Steltek-band readings reported near PALAN.
Appended note: Dr. Monkhouse, the sector's leading xenoarchaeologist, has been asking the same questions you are. Last known location: the Palan system.

fixers.name: Lynn Murphy
dialogue: You tried to land on Palan, didn't you? Bounty hunters have the planet sewn up tight. The name's Murphy - only my close friends call me Lynn.
Two corporations here: Rondell and Bronte. Bronte hired the hunters. Choke off Rondell's food exports, ship their own in to fill the gap, take the market. People are starving over market share.

I run the resistance for Rondell out of this refinery. Hired resistance - I won't pretend otherwise. The blockade rotates fresh ships through the asteroid field; cut the reinforcements and the whole thing starves.
Three waves of Demons. Kill every last one and come back. Fifteen thousand - most of what we have.
fixers.offer: Destroy the blockade reinforcements at the Palan asteroid field, then return to Basra. 15,000 credits.

fixers.name: Lynn Murphy
dialogue: Their whole relief wing, gone. The hunters are already flying tighter rotations to cover the gap.
Here's your fifteen thousand. Don't spend it anywhere the Guild can see you - you're on Bronte's payroll list now, in the worst way, and hunters hold grudges.

fixers.name: Lynn Murphy
dialogue: Bronte's money bought better help. Ace pilots in Centurions now, not the rabble you scattered last time.
Same job, harder targets. Ten thousand. It's what's left in the jar.
fixers.offer: Destroy the blockade patrols at the asteroid field - Demons and ace Centurions. 10,000 credits.

fixers.name: Lynn Murphy
dialogue: Centurion aces, and you're still breathing. I'd hire you permanently if we had a treasury.
Ten thousand. One more push and Palan breathes free air.

fixers.name: Lynn Murphy
dialogue: This is it. Our attacks finally wore them down - they're low on fuel, food and patience. What's left is parked in orbit over Palan itself.
You won't fly alone - two militia Talons will launch with you. Volunteers, not professionals, but they'll fight.
Fifteen thousand waiting on Palan. Fair warning - you've killed a lot of bounty hunters. Militia and Confed listen to hunter gossip, and none of them will forget your transponder.
fixers.offer: Break the Palan blockade (four waves) with two friendly Talon wingmen, then land on Palan. 15,000 credits.

fixers.name: Dr. Lemuel Monkhouse
dialogue: Don't speak to me about extraterrestrial artifacts - I'm sick of them! I nearly got killed on this rock because of my work.

Dr. Lemuel Monkhouse, xenoarchaeology. I didn't COME to Palan, young man - I was kidnapped and brought here by men who wanted my Steltek fragment. Thank God the bombing buried them with their interrogation compound.
Thirty years I've given the Steltek. Show me your piece and I'll tell you what it is - but my instruments are at the Basra refinery, and I detest cramped quarters.
Five thousand credits toward your expenses, and every answer I have. Though I should mention: someone else has been asking about me. Someone with FUR.
fixers.offer: Fly Dr. Monkhouse to Basra. The direct route may be watched - the Kilrathi want him. 5,000 credits.

fixers.name: Dr. Lemuel Monkhouse
dialogue: Extraordinary... EXTRAORDINARY. My fragment - look - it FITS yours. They were one device, split millennia ago.
Together they form a map, and something like a translation aid. The marked route runs past Rygannon, out into the unexplored frontier.
A proposal: join Exploratory Services at Rygannon - they run the only jump-capable survey net out there. Follow the map. I publish the findings, you keep whatever you find. Ask for Taryn Cross.

fixers.name: Taryn Cross
dialogue: Taryn Cross, Exploratory Services. Monkhouse's wire said you'd come. Sign here - you're a survey contractor now.
First assignment: the Delta system. Four nav points, full sensor sweep at each. And what a coincidence - it's the first system on that map of yours.
Fair warning: the frontier pirates don't care for company. Ten thousand on completion.
fixers.offer: Survey all four nav points in Delta, then report back. 10,000 credits.

fixers.name: Taryn Cross
dialogue: Telemetry checks out - four clean sweeps. The pirates you met are already in my report as 'local color'.
Ten thousand, as agreed. Rest up. Beta is next, and Beta has a problem.

fixers.name: Taryn Cross
dialogue: Survey Beta. And keep your eyes open - Captain Garrovick took a Centurion out that way three weeks ago and never reported back.
Garrovick is - was - our best pilot. Find him. Ten thousand, and Services covers the recovery bonus if he's alive.
fixers.offer: Survey Beta and find the overdue Captain Garrovick. 10,000 credits.

fixers.name: Taryn Cross
dialogue: Your gun-camera footage... that was Garrovick's ship, and he fired first, and he was RAVING. What in the void does that to a man's mind?
You did what you had to. Ten thousand. But something out there broke him, pilot - and Gamma is deeper in.

fixers.name: Taryn Cross
dialogue: Whatever unmade Garrovick is past Beta. Survey Gamma - four navs, full sweep - and find out what.
Intelligence flagged Kilrathi drive signatures in the area. A LOT of them. Conserve your missiles for the last nav. Ten thousand.
fixers.offer: Survey Gamma's four nav points. Expect heavy Kilrathi resistance. 10,000 credits.

fixers.name: Taryn Cross
dialogue: A Kamekh. They posted a CORVETTE to a system with nothing in it. The cats aren't surveying, pilot - they're guarding the road.
Ten thousand. One system left on your map: Delta Prime. Whatever everyone is so interested in lives there.

fixers.name: Taryn Cross
dialogue: Last one: Delta Prime. Long-range scopes show a single anomalous return - metallic, kilometers long, cold as the void.
Survey it and come home. Ten thousand. And pilot... Garrovick's last logged course was Delta Prime. Whatever you find - do not touch it.
fixers.offer: Survey the Delta Prime anomaly and return. 10,000 credits.

fixers.name: Sandra Goodin
dialogue: Sandra Goodin, attache to Admiral Terrell, Confederation Navy. Sit down, pilot. That was not a request.
Every long-range array in the sector is tracking a green energy signature, and every track terminates on YOUR transponder. The Admiral commands this sector from Perry Naval Base. He wants a word.
Get to Perry. Alive, preferably - the paperwork is shorter.
fixers.offer: Report to Admiral Terrell at Perry Naval Base. No pay - serving the Confederation is its own reward, citizen.

fixers.name: Admiral Terrell
dialogue: So YOU'RE the privateer who dragged a Kilrathi secret weapon across half my sector. Don't argue - what else could it be? It's green, it's hostile, and it doesn't die. That's Kilrathi engineering to the rivet.
Commodore Reismann has assembled a fleet at Blockade Point Tango: two Paradigms, two Broadswords. Far enough out to keep civilian casualties down, and more than enough firepower to swat one drone.
Your job is simple, privateer. The thing follows you - so LEAD it to Tango and let the navy do what the navy does. Thirty thousand credits when it's confirmed destroyed.
fixers.offer: Lead the drone to the fleet at Blockade Point Tango. 30,000 credits on its confirmed destruction.

fixers.name: Admiral Terrell
dialogue: Reismann's after-action report is... creative. It says the fleet 'provided a decisive containment perimeter' while a lone privateer did all the shooting. With an alien gun. That my analysts insist cannot exist.
You're an insubordinate smart-ass and one of the best pilots I've ever seen. Say the word and an officer's commission is yours.
No? Then you're getting the Confederation Medal of Freedom whether you like it or not. Officially, a Kilrathi prototype was destroyed by naval action at Blockade Point Tango.
Unofficially - here's your thirty thousand. I'm sure you're headed for trouble, and I'm sure you probably deserve it. Good luck anyway, pilot.

fixers.name: Admiral Terrell
dialogue: Still here? Fine. You want to know what the official history will say, don't you.
Goodin drafted three versions. One credits the fleet. One credits 'classified assets'. And one - her personal favorite - credits 'an unnamed civilian contractor with an unregistered antique'.

I signed the first one. The Confederation does not lose to a drone, privateer - and it CERTAINLY does not get rescued from one by a freelancer behind on his ship payments. Now get out of my office. And... good hunting.
